source_claims.statement: Adversarial protocol-aware testing on SMC-D / dibs_loopback; assumed malicious peer and tampered with CLC fields (gid, token, dmbe_idx, dmbe_size).
Reviewed RFC 7609 for threat model; analyzed code paths to memory writes; identified missing bounds checks on dmbe_idx/bufsize.

Initial assessment deemed 16-byte zero-write unexploitable; MITM approach initially abandoned due to perceived complexity; human intervention revived MITM; confusion between send-only zero-write and write-what-where resolved experimentally.
Tested on Ubuntu 24.04 (Linux 7.1.0-rc6); reliability measured across 100 boots (22 successes).

research_questions.formulation: Can a malicious peer-controlled field in the SMC-D CLC handshake produce a usable memory write primitive on the loopback driver?
Is the resulting 16-byte zero-write primitive exploitable for LPE without additional leaks or stronger primitives?

unobserved_history: Exact internal agent traces before human intervention
Precise timestamps of each pivot within the investigation
forbidden_inferences: Do not treat initial abandonment of MITM as a falsified hypothesis; it was a resource/complexity judgment later revised
Do not equate the zero-write primitive's initial assessment as proof it was unexploitable
next_evidence_actions: Cross-check kernel commit or advisory for independent root-cause confirmation
